# Results — Study 184 (Williams-Fractals) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Bill Williams' 5-bar
fractal pattern — a bar whose high (bearish fractal) or low (bullish fractal) is strictly
beyond the two bars on each side — is tested in two framings:*

*1. **Reversal**: fade the swing extreme (short after bearish fractal, long after bullish),
   enter at open of bar t+3 (2 bars after confirmation).  
2. **Breakout**: enter long on the first close above a bullish fractal high, short below
   a bearish fractal low, within 20 bars of confirmation.*

*Both are raced against a **random-direction control** on identical entry bars.  Six tickers
(SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT, GLD), 10 years of daily bars, pooled.  As-of **2026-06-15**.*

Fractals fire on ~26.8% of daily bars (bear: 2,014, bull: 2,029 across 6 tickers × 10 yr).

## Reversal framing — hold 5 days, gross

A bearish fractal (5-bar swing high) → short at open of bar t+3.
A bullish fractal (5-bar swing low) → long at open of bar t+3.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fractal reversal (signal)** | 3,988 | **49.7%** | **−4.09** | **−1.26** |
| Random direction (control) | 3,988 | 50.3% | +2.95 | +0.60 |

- The reversal gross expectancy is **−4.09 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−1.26** — no real
  edge, and if anything slightly negative.  The coin earns +2.95 bps, so the fractal
  *underperforms* a random guess by Δ = **−7.04 bps/trade**.
- This is the opposite of what the reversal theory predicts.  The 5-bar confirmation delay
  (2 bars) consumes most of any short-term reversion that actually occurs; the trade opens
  after the bounce, not into it.

| Ticker | n | win-rate | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 636 | 50.0% | +2.03 | +0.29 |
| QQQ  | 632 | 50.5% | −7.39 | −0.89 |
| IWM  | 670 | 51.6% | +3.01 | +0.36 |
| AAPL | 672 | 48.4% | −8.28 | −0.83 |
| MSFT | 684 | 49.1% | −15.93 | **−1.93** |
| GLD  | 694 | 48.8% | +2.16 | +0.37 |

No instrument clears |*t*| ≥ 2.  MSFT is the closest at −1.93 (a directional negative,
not a positive edge).  Mixed signs across instruments confirm noise, not signal.

## Breakout framing — hold 5 days, gross

After a confirmed bullish fractal (t+2), buy on the first close above the fractal high;
after a bearish fractal, sell on the first close below the fractal low. Active for up to 20 bars.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fractal breakout (signal)** | 3,346 | **50.5%** | **−0.06** | **−0.01** |
| Random direction (control) | 3,346 | 50.8% | +1.04 | +0.19 |

Essentially zero — the breakout is exactly a coin flip on daily bars.

## Hold-period sweep (reversal, gross)

| Hold | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 d  | 3,988 | −1.77 | −1.00 |
| 3 d  | 3,988 | −4.94 | −1.59 |
| 5 d  | 3,988 | −4.09 | −1.26 |
| 10 d | 3,988 | −1.60 | −0.42 |
| 20 d | 3,988 | +5.54 | +1.09 |

No hold period clears the inference bar.  The 3-day hold (*t* = −1.59) is the *most*
negative but still insignificant and in the wrong direction for a reversal trade.

## Cost sweep (reversal, hold=5)

| Round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −4.09 | −1.26 |
| 0.5 bps | −4.59 | −1.41 |
| 1.0 bps | −5.09 | −1.57 |
| 2.0 bps | −6.09 | −1.88 |
| 5.0 bps | −9.09 | **−2.80** |

At 5 bps (realistic for mid-cap names / active traders), the strategy is a statistically
significant loser (*t* = −2.80).  At 1 bp the gross edge is already negative, so there
is **no positive break-even cost** — the loss is structural, not killed by costs.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Both the reversal (HAC *t* = −1.26) and breakout (*t* = −0.01)
  framings are statistically indistinguishable from noise.  The reversal underperforms a
  random-direction control by 7 bps/trade; the breakout is a pure coin flip.  No instrument
  clears |*t*| ≥ 2.  The 5-bar pattern is a popular chart object that carries zero forward
  information once tested honestly against a random baseline.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A gross loss of −4 bps/trade compounds to a structurally
  negative outcome; at 5 bps the strategy is a high-confidence loser (*t* = −2.80).  The
  pattern fires on ~27% of all trading days, so turnover is also high.
- **Beat a coin? — No.** The fractal signal performs *worse* than a random-direction
  entry on the same bars in both framings.
